_about: PurTera's fixed handling per job type: SOW items a PM writes on every job of that type whether or not the deal states them (template content, not deal facts). Owner-reviewed. The writer writes every item unless a deal fact contradicts it. Sections match sow_method_library.json.

decommission_packing._source: owner, 2026-10-18 (010115 v1 grade: PM-habit items are PurTera standard handling); items added from the 010115 v1 TEMPLATE list (grade round 12)
method_steps: Meet the onsite contact on arrival and review the hardware to be dismantled and packed.
Assist with the physical disconnection of the equipment as directed by the onsite contact.
Dismantle the hardware and organize it for packing.
Pack the equipment in the customer-provided boxes and packing materials, labeling each box.
Package the equipment as instructed by the customer's representative.
Place the packed equipment in the customer's designated staging or shipment area.
Notify the onsite contact of any damage, missing materials or access issues.
Maintain a clean and orderly work area and remove packing debris.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Identify all hardware in scope for dismantling and packing.
Ensure the onsite contact or designated representative is available throughout the engagement.
Provide sufficient packing materials (boxes, pallets, tape and labels) onsite before the technician arrives.
Designate a staging or shipment area for the packed equipment.
Provide instructions for dismantling, packing, labeling, staging and shipment preparation.
Provide any additional security, dock or escort requirements before arrival.
Disconnect or arrange for the safe disconnection of any electrical, building, security, or specialized connections that require a licensed trade or manufacturer-authorized resource.
Accept responsibility for the transportation, shipment, storage, and disposal of all equipment and materials.
Ensure equipment is accessible and free from obstructions.
Provide any specialized tools, carts, pallets, shipping or lifting equipment the job needs.
assumptions: Equipment is powered down and released for removal before the technician arrives.
Onsite parking is available; any parking fee is reimbursable.
The engagement is limited to onsite physical labor and smart hands support.
The hardware can be safely dismantled using common hand tools.
No specialized lifting equipment or powered material handling equipment is required.
Services are limited to onsite smart hands support for the dismantle and packing.
exclusions: Transport, shipping or freight of packed equipment.
Hardware installation, configuration, programming, troubleshooting, data migration, network changes, or system testing.
Inventory audit, asset reconciliation, disposal, recycling, data destruction, or certified IT asset disposition.
Packing materials, transportation, shipping or disposal of equipment.
deliverable_outcomes: Hardware dismantled as directed by the onsite contact.
Equipment packed in customer-provided materials and labeled.
Packed equipment staged in the designated shipment area.
Damage, missing materials or access issues reported to the onsite contact.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact.
tools: Common hand tools, including screwdrivers and wrenches.

low_voltage_cabling._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic cabling handling from the 010082 v1 TEMPLATE list (job-specific hardware left to the deal); 010082 v2 grade TEMPLATE items (business-hours arrival, J-hook/Velcro support, metal-stud screws, drilling-prohibited areas, trenching/demolition/hazmat)
method_steps: {unless:after[- ]hours|overnight|weekends?\b|night shift} Arrive onsite during the Customer-approved regular business hours.
Review the work areas and the cable pathway with the onsite point of contact.
Confirm each mounting and termination location with the onsite point of contact before drilling or mounting equipment.
Use fastening methods suited to the existing wall and stud conditions, with anchors or toggle bolts where approved and no stud is available.
{when:metal studs?} Use self-tapping metal screws suited to the metal studs.
Verify each backboard, cabinet and mounted device is level and securely fastened.
Maintain proper cable support and never rest cable directly on ceiling tiles, electrical fixtures, plumbing or ductwork.
Support the cable using J-hooks, Velcro and other appropriate low-voltage cable supports.
Terminate and label each cable run at both ends.
Test each cable run for 4-pair continuity.
Inform the onsite point of contact of each cable's location.
Clean the immediate work area and remove Provider-generated installation debris.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Provide device and termination locations before the technician arrives.
{when:drill|mount|backboard|backing board} Identify any areas where drilling or mounting is prohibited.
assumptions: The work can be completed from an appropriate A-frame ladder; powered lifts, scaffolding or specialty access equipment are not included and may require a change order.
Final mounting methods are based on the existing wall conditions, available studs, equipment weight and customer approval.
The cable pathway is accessible and free from major obstructions.
exclusions: Electrical work, new power circuits or modification of existing power infrastructure.
Fire-stopping, core drilling, conduit installation or structural modification.
Network configuration, programming or active equipment setup.
Trenching, demolition or hazardous material remediation.
deliverable_outcomes: Cable runs installed, terminated and labeled at both ends.
Continuity test results for each run.
Completion photographs of terminations and visible cable routing.
tools: Wood, metal and masonry drill bits as conditions require.
Screwdrivers, hand tools and socket tools.
Labeling and basic cable management tools.
materials: Screws, anchors, washers and standard mounting hardware.
Standard low-voltage consumables, labels, tape and installation hardware.
J-hooks and standard low-voltage cable supports.
{when:metal studs?} Self-tapping metal screws suitable for metal studs.
